title: LBJ: The Play is playing Off-Off-Broadway at the Paradise Factory now...
transcript: Shows set in classrooms are kind of in right now. We just had Big Feelings, The immersive play where you assume the role of a first grader Finish up its second sold out run off Broadway, and now we have LBJ: the play where you assume the role of fifth grader whose teacher brings in a Lyndon B. Johnson impersonator to teach the class more about the 1960s. Now, this one is not immersive. It is done in a pretty traditional theatre setup and definitely has a much more comedic tone as the LBJ Impersonator has gone full method and is essentially using this presentation as a trial run for his new play, telling his life story and attempting to salvage his legacy. LBJ Is played by the playwright Sunny Zimmerman, and they're hamming it up every step of the way with this over the top performance that despite its best efforts, still manages to be genuinely educational. It's a little bit like Oh Mary where they've created this persona based on the concept of Lyndon B. Johnson. But the actual story being told is much more historically accurate. I am a little torn on the ending of this show, as there is a third act turn that I'm not sure really works. And the show is definitely at its best when it is leaning into the absurd. But I honestly had a really fun time with this show, and I am Going to say that this is a Broadway Ben recommendation, especially if you like these farcical takes on history, a la Oh Mary!
